name: Robin's Egg
lede: Robin's Egg is a bright, saturated cyan named for the bird's shell, recorded by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 and absent from our painting archive entirely.

sections.title: A bird's-egg blue, too bright for paint
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files this hue as block 186, a grayish blue, and the crowd-sourced xkcd color survey of 2010 records a close match under its own name [1]. The name points to the pale, saturated blue of a robin's eggshell, though our sources give no earlier printed record than the 1955 entry [1]. At chroma 36, it is one of the most saturated colors, well past what most historical paint pigments could reach [2].

The nearest named color is [[robin-s-egg-blue|Robin's Egg Blue]], a paler variant 4.0 units away [2]. [[sky-blue-crayola|Sky Blue (Crayola)]] sits 5.6 units off, [[bright-light-blue|Bright Light Blue]] is 5.9 units away, and [[aqua-blue|Aqua Blue]] is 6.1 units off [2]. In LCH terms Robin's Egg measures lightness 87, chroma 36, hue 211 degrees [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries Robin's Egg covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive's photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not painting as a whole: a color this bright and saturated rarely survives in old pigments or in centuries of varnish darkening [3]. It is best looked for in modern design and screens, where it is named for, rather than historical paintings [3].
